transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I made an appointment. I just... I guess I came in because I've started doing some things recently that kind of scare me a little bit? 

I'm usually very responsible—I'm a systems analyst, so I have to be—but lately I've just been... well, doing things that are really out of character. Like, I've been walking out in the middle of major software deployments at work. Or I'll just get in my car and drive around late at night with absolutely no plan. I know it sounds a bit silly, and it's probably just stress, but... that is just not how I’ve ever handled stress before. I thought I should probably talk to someone about it. Does that... does that sound like a good reason to be here?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge when you're not doing these out-of-character activities?

Um, well, yes, I suppose so. I hope it's okay to admit that, but... yeah, even on the quiet days, I just have this feeling sitting right here in my chest. It's... it's kind of a mix of fear and, um, maybe a little bit of shame? Like I really should have handled everything better, and if I let my guard down, something bad could still happen. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, and I'm really trying not to let it get to me, but it's just sort of always there. Is that... is that a normal way to feel when you're stressed?
Are there things or situations that you've been avoiding lately?

Um, avoiding? Well, maybe a little bit. I mean, I guess I've been... I've been taking the long way around the building at work. And I try to avoid the third floor whenever I can. It's just easier that way, you know? 

And, um, if people start talking about the new contractor or the big cutover we had, I just... I kind of shut the conversation down. I try to be polite about it, of course! I don't want to be rude to my coworkers. But I just change the subject as quickly as I can. 

I know it's probably silly to avoid those things, and I really should just deal with it like a professional. I hope you don't think less of me for that. Is it... is it okay that I'm doing that, just for now?
Has something specific and disturbing happened to you recently?

Um, well... I guess you could say something happened. I mean, it wasn't a war zone or anything, so I don't want to make it sound worse than it was. But... yeah, there was an incident. 

It was during a late-night cutover at work. A big system upgrade. It was... it was really bad. And, um, this whole thing—the avoiding the third floor, the walking out, feeling so on edge—it's all been going on since then. It's been a little over a year now, maybe about 13 months? 

I really thought I would have just bounced back by now, being a professional and all. I've tried so hard to just push through it and be normal. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining or being weak about something that happened that long ago. Do you... do you think it makes sense that I'm still struggling with it after a year?
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like things aren't real, especially when you're doing those out-of-character activities or thinking about the incident at work?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely get overwhelmed sometimes, but I always know I'm me, and I'm right there in the moment. I don't feel like I'm watching myself from the outside or anything strange like that. 

I just get really... intensely focused on whatever I'm doing, or I just feel that awful tightness in my chest. But everything still feels real, even if it's uncomfortable. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. I'm still very grounded, I promise.
Do you ever have memories or images of the incident at work that come into your mind when you don't want them to?

Um, well... yes, sometimes. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting around dwelling on it on purpose, I promise! I try really hard to stay focused on my work. But, um... yeah, sometimes they just pop up out of nowhere. 

Like, if I have to walk past that conference area, or even if someone just raises their voice a little bit on a conference call... I'll just suddenly get hit with these images and sounds from that night. It's so strong sometimes that I'll completely lose track of what I was saying in a meeting. 

I try to just smile and cover it up so nobody notices, because I really don't want to seem unprofessional or like I can't handle my job. It's just a little distracting, that's all. Is that... is that a normal thing to happen? I hope you don't think I'm just letting my imagination run away with me.
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?

Um... well, I guess sleep has been a little... tricky. I mean, I know everyone has bad nights, so I really shouldn't complain. But most nights, I just lie there in the dark and... I end up replaying pieces of that office incident over and over. 

I really try to clear my head and practice good sleep habits, I promise! But it just keeps coming back. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up feeling completely tense. Sometimes it's from a dream, or even just some small noise in the house will jolt me awake. 

So, I end up feeling pretty exhausted before work even starts. I always make sure to power through it and get my tasks done, though—I'd never let it affect my projects. I just drink a little extra coffee and put on a brave face. Do you think... is it normal to still be losing sleep over this? I just hope it doesn't sound like I'm not taking care of myself properly.
Do you feel guilty about what happened during the late-night cutover at work?

Um, guilty? Well... I mean, maybe a little bit? I know it wasn't technically my fault, and I really try to remind myself of that. I definitely don't want you to think I'm sitting around throwing a pity party or anything! 

But... yeah, I guess I do feel bad about it. Even on quiet days, when everything is going fine, I just have this... this mix of fear and shame sitting right here in my chest. It's like I can't shake the feeling that I should have handled everything better, you know? Like I should have seen it coming or reacted differently. 

And then there's this lingering feeling that something bad could still happen if I let my guard down for even a second. I try really hard to just push past it and stay positive, I really do. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm being overly dramatic? I just want to be honest with you so I'm doing this right.
Do you find yourself getting easily irritated or having a short temper lately?

Um, irritated? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to be patient with everyone. I know how stressful our work environment can be, so I always try to be the calm one in the room. 

I guess... well, maybe occasionally I might feel a tiny bit more on edge than usual? Like if there are too many people talking at once or if someone drops something heavy near my desk. But I would never snap at anyone or lose my temper! I always make sure to keep a smile on my face and just take a deep breath. 

I really don't want to be one of those difficult coworkers, you know? I pride myself on being easy to work with. So, no, I wouldn't say I have a short temper at all. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you been avoiding certain people or social situations since the incident at work?

Um... avoiding people? Well, I wouldn't say I'm being anti-social or anything! I still go to work every day and do my job, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just hiding away. 

But, um... I guess I have made a few little adjustments? Just to keep things running smoothly. Like, I've started taking the long way around the building when I come in. And I try to just... steer clear of that specific floor whenever I can. It's just easier that way, you know? Less distraction. 

And if people start talking about the contractor or the cutover... well, I usually just try to change the subject right away. I kind of shut down those conversations. Not to be rude! I just think it's better for everyone to focus on the present instead of dwelling on past projects. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm being difficult or uncooperative with my team.
Do you find yourself being constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when there's no apparent reason to be?

Um, constantly on the lookout? Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm a responsible person, so I pay attention to my surroundings, especially if I'm leaving the office late or something like that. But I definitely wouldn't say I'm expecting threats all the time! 

I really try to just trust my environment and assume the best. I wouldn't want to make anyone around me uncomfortable by acting... well, paranoid or jumpy, you know? I always try to just focus on my work and stay grounded. 

So, no, I haven't really noticed myself doing that. Is... is that a normal thing people experience? I hope it's okay that I don't have that one. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need to know.
Do you often find yourself being more alert to your surroundings than you used to be?

Um... more alert? Well, like I said before, I think I'm just being responsible. I definitely wouldn't say I'm, like, overly alert or anything like that. 

I mean, maybe I notice things a tiny bit more than I used to? Just little things, like where the exits are in a room, or who is walking behind me. But I think that's just being smart, right? Everyone should be a little aware of their surroundings. I don't want you to think I'm sitting at my desk scanning the room constantly or anything crazy like that! 

I really just try to go about my day normally and not let things get to me. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Has your behavior or these feelings been affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Um... my relationships? Well, I really try my hardest not to let anything spill over. I always want to be a good partner and a good teammate, you know? I don't want to inconvenience anyone. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—because I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need—there have been a couple of... little hiccups. 

Like at home, my husband is so wonderful, but he did say recently that it feels like I'm... barely present anymore. I think my mind just wanders, but I'm really trying to be better about being engaged for him, I promise! 

And, um... well, it has bled into work just a tiny bit. I had my performance review recently, and... it was actually the first one where I got some, um, less-than-perfect feedback. They told me I'm missing some key handoffs, and that I've been leaving meetings abruptly. They said it feels like the team is having to work around me right now. 

I felt absolutely terrible when they said that! I really, really don't want to be a burden to my team. I'm already taking steps to fix it so they don't think poorly of me. Is... is it normal to struggle a little bit like that? I just hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad wife or a terrible employee... I really am trying my best.
Have you felt like you're having trouble fulfilling your responsibilities at work or at home because of these feelings or behaviors?

Um... yes, I suppose so. I mean, I know I just mentioned this a second ago, but... yeah, it's definitely been a little harder lately to keep all the balls in the air. 

Like I said, the performance review was... well, it was really hard to hear. I've always prided myself on being a top performer, so being told I'm missing those key handoffs and... and leaving meetings abruptly... it just makes me feel awful that the team feels they have to work around me. I really don't want to be that kind of coworker. I'm trying so hard to fix it, I really am.

And then at home, with my husband saying I'm barely present... I just hate that I'm letting him down, too. I want to be a good wife and a good employee, but it just feels like I'm dropping things everywhere right now. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm sort of repeating myself from before. I just... I hope it's okay that I'm struggling with this a little bit? I really want to get back to being the reliable person everyone expects me to be. Is it... is it okay that I'm having a hard time with these things right now?
Have you felt like your relationships or work performance have been significantly impacted by your feelings or behaviors since the incident at work?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I know I keep bringing it up, and I'm really sorry to sound like a broken record... but yes, it has been significant, I suppose. 

I just... I really want you to know that I'm normally very dependable. But since... since everything happened, it's just been so hard to keep it all together. Like I mentioned, that performance review was a huge wake-up call. Hearing that I'm missing handoffs and just... walking out of meetings... and that they feel like they have to work around me... it's just not who I am. I hate that I'm putting that on them. 

And my husband... he's so patient, but when he said I'm barely present... that really hurt, because I want to be there for him. I don't want to be a bad wife or a bad coworker. 

So, yes, I guess it has impacted things significantly. I'm really trying to turn it around, though! I'm taking all this seriously. I hope you don't think less of me for letting things slip like this... I just want to get back to normal. Does that make sense?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... lost interest? Well... I mean, I still *like* the things I used to do, I really do! I just... I haven't been doing them quite as much lately. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being lazy or anything, I promise I'm not! 

It's just... I used to be so active, you know? I would plan my whole week around going to salsa dancing, or my book club, or yoga... and I loved having people over to cook Guatemalan food for them. I really pride myself on being a good host. 

But lately... um, if I'm being perfectly honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information—I've been canceling a lot. I usually just end up sitting at home... scrolling on my phone or, you know, putting a show on but not really watching it. Just sort of pretending to. 

I feel so guilty about it, especially when I cancel on my friends. I really don't want to be a flake. I'm hoping I can get back to all those things soon, because I know it's important to stay active and social. Is it... is it normal to just sort of step back from things for a little bit when you're going through a hard time? I just hope I'm not doing this all wrong...
Do you ever feel disconnected from yourself or the world around you?

Um... disconnected? I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I know I just said I've been sitting at home a lot and not really engaging with things, but... I don't feel disconnected from *myself*. 

I know who I am, and I'm still here, you know? I'm just... maybe a little distracted lately. But I definitely don't feel like I'm floating away or that things aren't real. I'm very grounded, I promise. I try really hard to stay present, even if I'm just sitting on the couch. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be clear that I'm not... I don't know, losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm still me. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, even when you're in the middle of doing something?

Um... spaced out? No, I don't think I do. I mean, I know I said earlier that I get a little distracted sometimes, but I definitely wouldn't say I'm ever in a daze. 

With my job—I'm a computer systems analyst—I really have to keep my head in the game, you know? It requires a lot of concentration. So I try very, very hard to stay focused when I'm in the middle of doing something. I don't want you to think I'm just checking out or ignoring my responsibilities. I really pride myself on being sharp and on top of things. 

So, no, no dazes or anything like that. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need... I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can with all your questions.
